chunks: What al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd narrated from Muḥammad ibn Sinān, from Ibn Miskān, from Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār, from one who informed him, from him, peace be upon him, who said:
Pray the two rakʿahs during the time between where you are and when the light comes level with your head; then when it is after that, begin with the Fajr prayer.

key_terms.الرَّكْعَتَيْنِ: the two rakʿahs performed before the obligatory Fajr salat
key_terms.الضَّوْءُ: the light of dawn as a marker for prayer timing
key_terms.الْفَجْرِ: the Fajr salat, the obligatory dawn prayer
key_terms.بِحِذَاءِ: level with or aligned with, indicating a positional time sign
key_terms.رَأْسِكَ: your head, used here as a reference point for the height of the dawn light
key_terms.فَابْدَأْ: then begin, indicating priority of the obligatory prayer after that point

ai.seo_question: Until when can the two rakʿahs before Fajr be prayed before beginning the Fajr salat?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about the time for the two rakʿahs of Fajr. It indicates that these two rakʿahs are to be performed before the light rises to a certain level, and after that point one should begin with the Fajr salat.
